title: Jerusalem (Psalm 122)
hookLine: Yom Yerushalayim marks 1967 for many; everyone can pray "the peace of Jerusalem"
tomorrow: Shavuot: a wedding at the mountain

cards: Three times a day, in the standing prayer, Jews ask for Jerusalem to be rebuilt. At the end of a wedding, a glass is broken, and many say it's for Jerusalem.
At the end of the Passover seder and of Yom Kippur, people say: next year in Jerusalem. For almost two thousand years, most Jews who said that had never seen the city, and never would.
And there's a short psalm, only nine verses, that pilgrims sang on their way up the hills to it. One line in it is a request anyone, anywhere, can make.

teach.b: Psalm 122 is a Song of Ascents, one of fifteen psalms with that heading; many scholars think pilgrims sang them on the way up to Jerusalem for the festivals.

teach.h: LET US GO UNTO THE HOUSE.
teach.b: It begins with arrival, in the old Jewish translation: "I rejoiced when they said unto me: 'Let us go unto the house of the LORD.'" Then the pilgrims stand inside the gates.
Then the line people know: "Pray for the peace of Jerusalem; may they prosper that love thee. Peace be within thy walls."
In Hebrew: sha'alu shalom Yerushalayim. Shalom and Yerushalayim sound alike, and the psalm plays on it again and again. The rabbis noticed the name, too.
A midrash says Abraham called the place Yireh, God will see, and Shem, Noah's son, called it Shalem, whole.
So God, not wanting to offend either righteous man, joined the names: Yerushalayim, a city whose name holds seeing and wholeness. In modern times, Jerusalem has its own day.
Yom Yerushalayim, on the twenty-eighth of Iyar, marks June 1967, when, during the Six-Day War, Israeli forces took the Old City and Jews could again pray at the Western Wall.
For many, especially religious Zionists, it's a day of thanksgiving, with Hallel. Others don't mark it, or mark it with mixed feelings, because the city's future is still disputed.
Jerusalem is holy to Christians and Muslims too, and home to all of them. That's why the psalm's line lasts. It doesn't ask who should hold the city.

how: Psalm 122 is recited among the Songs of Ascents, often on Shabbat afternoons in winter; on Yom Yerushalayim, many religious Zionist communities add Hallel and festive prayers, while other communities do not mark the day.

games.q: Abraham called the place Yireh. Shem called it Shalem. in the midrash, what does God do?
games.why: not wanting to slight either righteous man, God joined them: Yerushalayim.

practice: If you can, find Psalm 122 and read its nine verses slowly; if not, just repeat its middle line: pray for the peace of Jerusalem. Then hold the city in mind, its stones, its streets, the people of every faith who live there today.
If you pray, this is a line you can pray; if you don't, simply wish them peace.

wordCard.voice: Jerusalem. Yerushalayim, the city of the Songs of Ascents, whose name the psalm plays on: shalom, peace. Today's word.
